ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (creation of UIAF); Ley 1121 de 2006 (AML/CFT framework for non-financial sectors); Ley 1258 de 2008 (S.A.S. regime); Ley 2155 de 2021 (mandatory beneficial owner reporting); Resolución UIAF 164 de 2022 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUBF); Decreto Único Reglamentario 1068 de 2015; Decreto 1074 de 2015 (commercial registry and chamber of commerce tariffs); Circular Básica Jurídica of the Superintendencia Financiera.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of certificate of incorporation and legal representation of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent competent authority in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (preferred); consular legalization at a Colombian consulate for non-Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized special power of attorney (poder especial) appointing the Colombian incorporation agent and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners and directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin or Colombian notary for domestic appointees
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for foreign documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and no criminal record (antecedentes penales) for each director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Police of Colombia or competent criminal records authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; Colombian certificates need no apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds of the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating financial institution in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature; accepted by Colombian notary and UIAF as part of the KYC file

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN list (Lista Clinton as recognized domestically), United Nations Security Council consolidated list, EU CFSP asset-freeze list, Colombian judicial asset forfeiture lists, and the national politically exposed persons (PEP) database implemented under Ley 2013 de 2019. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required where any UBO is a PEP, where the counterparty is domiciled in a high-risk jurisdiction, or where ownership involves non-transparent intermediaries. Screening results must be documented and retained for at least ten years per the RUBF and UIAF record-keeping standards.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) at https://www.rues.org.co, operated jointly with the relevant Cámara de Comercio; the name pre-clearance is evidenced by the Certificado de Homonimia issued by the local Chamber of Commerce.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Spanish or transliterated into the Latin-script Spanish alphabet; it may not be identical or strikingly similar (homonimia) to an existing company or trademark registered in Colombia. The name must be followed by the words 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada' or the initials 'S.A.S.' in accordance with Ley 1258 de 2008. The name must not mislead as to the actual corporate purpose or suggest a regulated financial activity without the corresponding authorization.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal (recurso de reposición) before the Cámara de Comercio within ten business days of notification, per the general administrative procedure under Ley 1437 de 2011. If the Chamber confirms the rejection, the applicant may file a second appeal (recurso de apelación) with the Superintendencia de Sociedades or, where applicable, seek judicial review before the Consejo de Estado within four months. Alternatively, the applicant may simply resubmit a new name clearance request under a materially distinct name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible. The S.A.S. must declare a real, verifiable physical address within a Colombian municipality as its registered seat (domicilio social). A commercial virtual office provider that maintains a physical street address and receives official correspondence is generally accepted by the Cámara de Comercio; however, a mere post office box or purely digital address is rejected. For a licensed real estate fund or REIT-style regulated activity, the Superintendencia Financiera expects a substantive local operational presence with physical premises and locally based compliance staff.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the passive real estate holding entity: approximately 10% probability per annum of an unannounced inspection by the Cámara de Comercio or DIAN in the absence of regulatory flags. The likelihood increases to 30-50% if the entity becomes subject to financial supervision, fails to maintain updated SARLAFT documentation, or triggers DIAN tax audit alerts. Regulatory findings may also trigger joint UIAF inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Code (Decreto 410 de 1971), Articles 98-128 and 471-490; Law 1258 de 2008 (SAS), Articles 1-48, especially Articles 5, 17-22, 25-28; Decree 1074 de 2015 (Regulatory Decrees of Commerce), Articles 2.2.1.1 et seq.; Single Business Registry (RUES) regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce) of the registered office, operating through the Single Business Registry (RUES); supervised by Superintendencia de Sociedades.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Private incorporation document (Documento Privado de Constitución) with bylaws filed in the Mercantile Registry; public deed (Escritura Pública) is required when in-kind contributions include immovable property or rights that require public formality.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Colombian SAS; the bylaws may provide for deferred payment terms. No escrow account is required for cash contributions. For in-kind contributions, a sworn inventory and appraisal must be annexed to the incorporation instrument; if real estate is contributed, title must be transferred by public deed before registry filing. For regulated real-estate collective investment activities, capital subscriptions are held through a fiduciary administration contract under Decree 2555 de 2010.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a duly convened founders’ meeting of [COMPANY] SAS, held in [CITY] on [DATE], the following resolutions were adopted unanimously: (1) the authorized share capital of COP [AMOUNT] is subscribed and accepted as set out in the schedules; each founder subscribes [NUMBER] shares of nominal value COP [AMOUNT], and the capital payment terms comply with Law 1258 of 2008, Art. 25; (2) the registered office and legal domicile are adopted as [ADDRESS], [CITY], Colombia; (3) [NAME] is appointed General Manager and legal representative and [NAME] as Secretary; (4) the General Manager is authorized to process the mercantile registration, NIT, permits and bank accounts. This resolution is effective upon incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Review and Bylaw Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search and obtain the certificate of homonymy (certificado de homonimia) to ensure the proposed name is distinguishable. Prepare the private incorporation document and bylaws, including the permitted corporate purpose referencing real-estate asset management, capital provisions, and management structure.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected or conflicts with an existing mark, file a new name request without incurring substantive fee; no formal appeal is needed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (if public deed is required) or founders collectively
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the incorporation document before the competent Notary if contributions include real estate or rights requiring public deed. Otherwise, all founders may execute a private document. Include appraisals and tax certificates for in-kind real estate contributions.
required_dossiers: Founders’ identification documents and tax IDs
Sworn inventory and appraisal of in-kind contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial defects or missing signature legalization are cured by replying to the notary and resubmitting the corrected deed; the chamber will not register a deed containing inaccuracies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the incorporation document, completed registration forms (Registro Único Empresarial), and proof of payment of registry fees and registration tax for the first year. Submit online or physically at the corresponding Chamber window.
required_dossiers: Formulario de matrícula mercantil and RUES basic form
Public deed or private document with notarized signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect notice, cure within the administrative term by correcting the documents and re-filing; failure to cure causes rejection, after which a new application is filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (National Tax and Customs Administration) - www.dian.gov.co
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain and verify the business taxpayer number (NIT); update the RUT electronically with the legal representative and registered office. The Chamber of Commerce may transmit preliminary data, but the company officer must accept the registration by signing the RUT.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence and representation issued by the Chamber of Commerce
Legal representative’s citizenship card or foreign ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects incomplete address or activity codes, correct the electronic form and re-file; discrepancies in CIIU classification are cured by using the exact ISIC 6499 / NAICS 525930 description.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation and Capital Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company’s name after chamber registration. Deposit cash subscriptions in accordance with the bylaws. If the entity plans REIT operations, subscribe units through a regulated fiduciary investment vehicle under Decree 2555 de 2010.
required_dossiers: Bylaws and identification of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional beneficial-ownership information, submit final beneficiary declarations and a corporate diagram; comply with account-opening AML/KYC requirements to avoid delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia de Sociedades; administrative registry windows
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Record appointments of officers, register beneficial owners under the beneficial-ownership reporting obligation, and file the relevant corporate acts in the Chamber of Commerce. Establish corporate governance and anti-money-laundering policies if the entity will act as a financial-manager vehicle.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Superintendency or registry returns the filing, correct the corporate book registration and resubmit through the RUES virtual window; a timely appeal to the registry body may be filed within the legal term.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (if operating as a regulated REIT/collective investment scheme); municipal planning office and Curaduría Urbana for land-use/construction permits; Ministry of Environment and Regional Autonomous Corporations for environmental licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Urban/land-use operating permit and occupancy certificate (Licencia de Urbanismo y Construcción / Certificado de Uso del Suelo), municipal business operating permit (Licencia de Funcionamiento), and, if a regulated vehicle, financial authorization from the Financial Superintendence.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: National Environmental Licensing Authority (ANLA) within the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development; regional environmental authority (Corporación Autónoma Regional - CAR) for local projects
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: REIT asset-management or lease activities involving existing buildings are generally subject to environmental registration or are exempt from a full EIA; a full environmental impact assessment is required only for new construction or projects in protected areas that meet the thresholds of Decree 1076 de 2015.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must comply with Resolution 0631 de 2015 parameter limits; air emissions and VOC abatement under Resolution 909 de 2008 and Resolution 2254 de 2017; solid and hazardous waste handling under Decree 4741 de 2005 and Law 1252 de 2008; noise standards for real estate operations under Resolution 0627 de 2006.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire department; structural load and electrical installation inspection certificates for buildings; occupational health and safety registration with an ARL if employees are hired; accessibility and occupancy certificates required by municipal planning authorities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax and Customs Directorate of Colombia (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales – DIAN), operating the MUISCA electronic portal (https://www.muisca.dian.gov.co) and the institutional portal (https://www.dian.gov.co).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must obtain a Colombian Tax Identification Number (NIT) by appointing a legal representative resident in Colombia and submitting the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) pre-registration through the MUISCA portal, attaching certified incorporation documents, a valid power of attorney, and the representative's identity documentation. The DIAN assigns the NIT and simultaneously classifies the taxpayer for income tax and VAT responsibilities; a SAS could obtain its NIT directly at formation under the DIAN's procedural rules with digital authentication.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not have a check-the-box or hybrid election regime. A SAS is a resident entity taxed at the entity level on its worldwide income. No transparent or pass-through election is available; taxpayers may only choose between the general corporate regime and the small-business 'Simples' regime when satisfying quantitative eligibility thresholds, which does not alter entity-level character for income tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: COP 164,727,500 (3,500 UVT for tax year 2024; UVT value COP 47,065). Mandatory registration as a VAT-responsible person results from exceeding this prior-year gross income threshold out of taxable activities, or from importing goods, holding taxable inventory, or performing categories of services regardless of threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) applies to all VAT-responsible and income-tax-registered entities: each invoice must be generated by DIAN-certified software and transmitted to DIAN in near real-time via authorized web-service providers for automated fiscal validation and the issuance of the unique electronic billing code (CUFE/CUDS). Export invoices must bear the validated CUFE and reference the underlying customs documentation; digital stamping and QR verification are integral.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Tangible goods qualify for a 0% (excluded) VAT rate where they are physically shipped and covered by a registered customs export declaration. Services qualify for 0% VAT where the beneficiary has no domicile or establishment in Colombia, the service is effectively used outside Colombia, and a service-export declaration (declaración de exportación de servicios) is filed. Real estate leases and sales of Colombian real property are statutorily excluded from VAT (Art. 476, E.T.), not export-zero-rated, so REIT rental income is VAT-exempt but requires RUT registration for income tax withholding duties.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación – DEX)
Transport Document (Bill of Lading or Air Waybill)
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Operation Report (Informe de Cambio y Certificado de Liquidación de Divisas)
Validated Electronic Export Invoice (Factura Electrónica de Exportación with CUFE)
Service-Export Contract and Supporting Performance Evidence (for service export zero-rating)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN may audit export files retroactively for up to five tax years and claw back refunded VAT plus default interest when the documentation is incomplete, inconsistent, or electronically untraceable; sanctions include (i) a 10% penalty for improper refund claims (Art. 647 E.T.), (ii) late-payment interest and monetary sanctions of up to 160% of the assessed tax (Art. 648 E.T.), and (iii) criminal liability of 48–108 months imprisonment plus fines of 260%–400% of the value fraudulently obtained (Art. 371-2 E.T.).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia) is the monetary and exchange-control authority, exercising prudential and exchange regulatory powers jointly with the Comité de Cambios (Foreign Exchange Committee) and the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia as the banking and AML supervisor. The binding exchange framework is set out in Ley 31/1992 and the comprehensive 'Régimen de Cambios Internacionales' implemented by Circular Reglamentaria Externa DCIN-83, administered and enforced by Banco de la República and DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) in their respective capacities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia maintains a free-float, market-based convertibility regime in which neither current-account nor capital-account operations require prior administrative exchange authorization. Current-account convertibility (dividends, profit remittances, service fees, interest and royalties) is unrestricted provided that the underlying foreign investment is registered in the Registro de Inversiones Internacionales (RII) of Banco de la República, the corresponding Declaración de Cambio (Form 1/Form 2) is submitted through an authorized intermediary ('intermediario del mercado cambiario', IMC), and local tax obligations (dividend withholding at source, ICA duties and corporate income tax) have been satisfied. Capital-account convertibility (equity injections, loans, unit redemptions, and property disposals) is likewise open but requires contemporaneous or ex-post RII registration and mandatory channeling through an IMC. The key remittance hurdles are procedural rather than discretionary: the investor must evidence the registered investment certificate, the corporate distribution minutes, and the tax payment/withholding certificates before the bank releases the wire; there is no ceiling on dividend conversion or prior approval quota.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Circular DCIN-83, exporters of goods and services must 'channel' export proceeds through an IMC or into a Banco de la República-registered foreign-currency compensation account (cuenta de compensación) within the following statutory windows: goods exports, six months from the customs shipment (fecha de embarque) date; services exports, six months from the contractual payment due date, or if none is stated, from service completion. For the nearshore software R&D and digital-customer-service revenue streams of the REIT, 100% of the foreign-currency consideration must be repatriated within that window. There is no fixed mandatory surrender ratio of USD to COP; the exporter may elect to sell the currency to the IMC (standard route) or deposit it in a registered compensation account, subject to quarterly reporting in the Declaración de Cambio. Failure to channel within the deadline, use of unregistered intermediaries, or late filing gives rise to administrative sanctions and pecuniary fines of up to 200% of the uncanalized value under the Régimen Cambiario.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul._compliance_notes: For the REIT, all dividend distributions to foreign unit holders must pass through the RII registration certificate of the original capital injection; the 12-month registration window for each capital contribution must be strictly monitored to avoid blockage of subsequent remittances. Currency conversion is executed at the official market rate (TRM) of the business day, with the bank issuing the corresponding exchange declaration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul._cross_reference: See Stage_1 corporate registration and Stage_2 tax characterization for the NIT/RUT and DIAN residency evidence required by the IMC during onboarding and each FX operation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (cuenta de garantía) and Operational Current Account in COP with a USD-denominated integrated settlement account
Operational Current Account in COP/USD; escrow and fiduciary-linked accounts through Fiduciaria Bogotá
Operational Current Account in COP and USD foreign-currency account; capital-guarantee escrow facility
Operational Current Account in COP and USD; global transfer and liquidity-sweep accounts

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Itaú Colombia S.A. (formerly Itaú Corpbanca Colombia)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Current Account in COP/USD and fiduciary-escrow deposit windows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury or clearing rail. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Mercury, Payoneer, Airwallex, N26-type platforms) are not licensed as Colombian IMCs and cannot lawfully execute the 'canalización' of export proceeds, capital contributions, or cross-border payments required by DCIN-83. Using them for equity injections or service-export revenue would constitute an unregistered foreign-exchange operation with DIAN and Banco de la República enforcement exposure. Their permissible role is limited to de minimis operational subscriptions (e.g., low-value SaaS and platform overhead) funded from IMC-cleared COP or USD balances; such usage should be expressly excluded from the bank covenant list to avoid inadvertent exchange-control violations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, the principal legal representative and the significant beneficial owners of the REIT must attend a physical KYC/SARLAFT interview at the selected bank's headquarters (Bogotá, Medellín, Cali or Barranquilla) before account activation. For non-resident directors, banks generally accept a notarized and apostilled 'poder general' (power of attorney) appointing a resident Colombian agent or corporate officer who attends the in-person interview, supplemented by video-assisted verification of the foreign principals' identification documents, passports, and residency records. Purely remote onboarding is not accepted for a first-time foreign-owned S.A.S.; at least one physical attendance by the appointed representative is mandatory in the majority of Tier-1 institutions, after which subsequent operations may be managed digitally.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: 100% foreign ownership with non-resident directors and an opaque investor-pool ownership chain typical of a REIT
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled corporate constitution and current Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal issued by the Chamber of Commerce within 90 days; full legal-entity structure chart down to natural persons; sworn Declaración de Beneficiario Final per DIAN Resolution 165/2022 and Law 2195/2022, together with the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB) filing receipt; passport copies, professional background, and source-of-wealth statements for each UBO holding 5% or more; clean PEP/sanctions screening outputs from a licensed provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: REIT/fiduciary wrapper receiving capital from a collective investment pool or managed accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Private placement memorandum or investment term sheet; the REIT or trust/fiducia deed and its regulations; bank statements of each material subscriber evidencing the provenance of funds; tax-status certificate or legal opinion from Colombian counsel confirming the REIT taxation classification and absence of unlicensed collective portfolio activity; audited or reviewed financial statements of the vehicle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound international wires arriving in rapid succession for real-property acquisitions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-submitted FX transaction instruction file quoting purpose code 2111 (direct investment for real-estate acquisition); copies of the notarial purchase agreement or title-escrow instructions for the target property; the Form 3 investment registration application filed with Banco de la República and the bank's adherence letter; a letter from the foreign investor confirming the clean source of funds and the nexus to the real-estate closing, with supporting bank references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name hits on sanctions/PEP lists or adverse regulatory news involving the REIT or its sponsors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent World-Check or Refinitiv screening results for the entity, all directors, and UBOs; sworn PEP-status declarations with reasoned explanations for any public-office exposure; a remedial legal opinion and reputational due diligence report adopted by the board; an engagement letter with the bank's compliance officer setting out enhanced monitoring and periodic refresh commitments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of physical presence, no local office or employees, and remote-only management intent
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered commercial address with a Colombian corporate agent or leased office space; a duly empowered resident legal representative with a notarized 'poder especial' expressly granted for KYC and banking operations; commitment letter for quarterly physical visits to the bank; provision of NIT, RUT, and paid-in social-capital certificates evidencing material economic activity and ongoing operation of the nearshore service center.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Each foreign equity contribution to the REIT follows a strict five-step protocol: (1) pre-funding the entity opens an operational COP current account and, optionally, a registered USD foreign-currency compensation account with an IMC; the foreign investor pre-files Form 3 'Declaración de Registro de Inversión Internacional' with Banco de la República, including the projected capital amount and property acquisition plan; (2) wire transmission the investor sends a SWIFT MT103 from a non-resident bank account in the investor's own name to the IMC, quoting purpose code 2111 (direct investment for the acquisition of real estate) and referencing 'Registro de Inversión Internacional – REIT S.A.S.'; funds must not be labeled as a loan or as a third-party collection; (3) conversion and credit the bank purchases the USD at the official TRM of the business day, credits the net COP proceeds to the operational account, and files the Declaración de Cambio (Form 1) on T+0/T+1; if a USD account is used, the funds are credited to the compensation account and reported quarterly; (4) registration the IMC issues the Certificado de Registro de Inversión Internacional and the final RII registration must be completed within twelve months of settlement, failing which dividend remittances and capital exits are blocked; and (5) utilization the COP balances are transferred to the property-purchase escrow or paid directly to the notary/title vendor via domestic transfer, preserving an audit trail that connects the specific inbound wire to the asset acquisition.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury flows settle through four principal rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 wires for dividends, intercompany management fees, software subcontracting, and vendor payments; each disbursement requires a Form 10/Form 11 remittance declaration, the underlying investment-registration certificate, distribution minutes, and withholding-tax certificates, with the bank selling COP against USD at the TRM through the IMC channel; (ii) commercial documentary letters of credit (MT700 issuance, MT707 amendment) and standby LCs for imported fit-out, hardware, and equipment, settled via MT103/MT202 cover payments from the issuing bank's USD account; (iii) ACH and CUD (Cámara de Compensación Urbana) domestic clearing for COP distributions to resident Colombian shareholders, rent remittances, payroll for the digital-customer-service center, and tax payments to DIAN and municipal authorities; and (iv) compensation-account sweeps and telegraphic transfers for overseas property managers and foreign suppliers, subject to quarterly Banco de la República reporting. All outbound payments remain subject to the channeling obligation where they involve repatriation of export proceeds, and to the five-year documentary retention requirement of the Régimen Cambiario.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: COP/USD deliverable forward (forward en TRM) traded with an IMC bank, permitted only where the entity holds a verifiable underlying real-economy exposure (USD-denominated property debt or USD service-export receivables) as required by Circular DCIN-83.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on COP against USD with authorized onshore or offshore counterparties, admissible when the REIT evidences an underlying transactional exposure and the bank records the corresponding declaration.
Cross-currency swap (swap de monedas) converting USD-denominated property loans into COP-linked cash flows, or vice versa, through IMC-approved counterparties.
European-style foreign-exchange options (call/put on COP/USD) for covered hedging positions with a domestic or international bank authorized to operate in Colombia.
Spot FX transactions (T+0/T+1) executed through the IMC for immediate operational liquidity management and rental-income conversion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail._settlement_calendar: Inbound wires from the US/offshore investor base typically settle T+1; local ACH and CUD credit transfers settle T+0. Dividends to foreign shareholders should be batched on a fixed quarterly calendar to align FX declarations, RII reporting, and tax withholding deadlines.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail._bank_account_priority: Open the Bancolombia or Banco de Bogotá pair first (Primary Operating + Escrow); the second bank serves as a redundant IMC clearing channel and FX pricing benchmark.

_treasury_risk_register.fx_risk: COP/USD volatility on USD-denominated property debt and service-export revenues; maintain continuous hedge coverage of at least 70% of net USD exposure using deliverable forwards and swaps.
_treasury_risk_register.liquidity_risk: Inbound capital windows of 12 months for RII registration; restrict distribution declarations until bank receipt and TRM conversion are fully documented.
_treasury_risk_register.regulatory_risk: Unchanneled proceeds, untimely Form 1/Form 2 filings, or use of unregistered EMIs trigger fines and blocked remittances; the compliance calendar must align with Banco de la República quarterly reporting dates.
_treasury_risk_register.aml_risk: The REIT's investor-pool structure requires a standing, refreshed UBO dossier and source-of-funds archive for every capital call and dividend distribution.

stage_4._governance_and_review_notes: This treasury blueprint will be reviewed quarterly by the board and the Colombian legal counsel, or upon any change in the ownership structure, banking counterparty, or FX regulation announced by Banco de la República or the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia.

_authoring_ai.disclaimer: This document is a structured compliance blueprint for internal treasury use and does not constitute legal advice. Independent Colombian counsel must confirm all statutory references, registration deadlines, and bank-specific KYC documentary requirements before execution.
_authoring_ai.output_language: Pure professional English with mandatory Spanish regulatory terms embedded for local filing accuracy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of Commercial Registration (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of each calendar year (renewal window runs January 1 – March 31; no anniversary rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a 10% monthly surcharge on the applicable registration tariff; continued failure may inactivate the commercial registration, block shareholder transfers and eventually lead to administrative strike-off of the S.A.S.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Deposit (Depósito de Estados Financieros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days following their approval by the shareholders' meeting, which must be held by March 31 of the year following the fiscal year-end (regular calendar year deadline: April 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-deposit or late deposit allows the Chamber to impose corrective fines (commonly up to USD 1,200) and can prevent registration of share transfers or amendments; sustained failure may be treated as non-compliance justifying strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing dates are set annually by DIAN Resolution based on the last digits of the NIT; for a calendar-year entity the return is generally due between April and June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a penalty of 5% of the income tax due for each month or fraction of month of delay, capped at 100% of the tax due; if no tax is due, a fixed fine is levied under the Colombian Tax Code (Estatuto Tributario), plus monetary correction and default interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in May (exact deadline assigned by DIAN Resolution according to NIT classification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccurate filing exposes the entity to a fine of up to 15,000 UVT (approx. USD 13,000) or to a penalty equivalent to 3% of the value of unreported payments, whichever is greater, in addition to criminal liability for intentional non-disclosure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficiary Registry Confirmation (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Chamber of Commerce and Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero (UIAF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the commercial registration renewal; must be confirmed by March 31 of each calendar year and updated within one month of any change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm the beneficiary registry renders the commercial renewal invalid and may result in fines imposed by the Superintendency of Companies (up to USD 4,000 for the company, USD 800 for each responsible director), and administrative strike-off for a closed S.A.S.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit by a Colombian Certified Public Accountant (Revisor Fiscal) applies if at the prior fiscal year-end the S.A.S. has total assets equal or greater than 5,000 monthly minimum legal wages (approx. USD 1,400,000), gross annual revenue equal or greater than 3,000 monthly minimum legal wages (approx. USD 840,000), or more than 15 employees; REIT activities classified as regulated financial vehicles may be subject to Superintendencia Financiera audit rules regardless of these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian Financial Information Standards (CFIS) issued under Law 1314 of 2009, aligned with IFRS as issued by the IASB; the S.A.S. will apply the technical framework applicable to its size group (Group 1 for public-interest or large entities, Group 2 for most medium and large S.A.S., Group 3 for small companies).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A.S. must file and confirm a Final Beneficiary Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) with the Cámara de Comercio each year during the March 1–31 renewal period, identifying every natural person that directly or indirectly holds at least 5% of share capital, voting rights, or control; the registry must be updated within 30 days after any share transfer or control change, and the annual confirmation is mandatory for the commercial registration to remain active.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Shareholders' Meeting Minutes (Libro de Actas de Asamblea)
Register of Board of Directors' Minutes (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva)
Minutes of the Statutory Auditor or Audit Committee (Libro de Actas de Revisoría Fiscal)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – 1,200 per year for a registered office and local commercial agent in Bogotá or Medellín
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 15,000 per year, depending on asset size and REIT distribution complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (Article 240 E.T., applicable to taxable year 2024 and onwards for Sociedades por Acciones Simplificadas)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No REIT-specific exemption in Colombia. Effective rate may be reduced through deductible operational expenses, mortgage interest subject to thin-cap rules, straight-line depreciation on buildings, property taxes, and amortisation of improvements; capital losses from disposal of investment properties may be offset only against occasional gains and carry forward up to 5 years.
